questions.question: Which of the following is not self-luminous?
questions.explanation: A self-luminous body emits light of its own. The moon only reflects light from the sun; it does not produce its own light. The incandescent bulb, fluorescent tube, lighted candle, and the sun all produce their own light.

questions.question: What are cathode rays?
questions.explanation: Cathode rays are streams of fast-moving electrons emitted from the cathode (negative electrode) in a discharge tube. They are deflected by electric and magnetic fields, confirming they are negatively charged particles.

questions.question: The electrochemical equivalent of silver is 0.0012g/C. If 36.0g of silver is to be deposited by electrolysis on a surface by passing a steady current for 5mins, the current must be?
Calculate the change in volume when 90g of ice is completely melted. [density of water = 1g cm<sup>-3</sup>, density of ice = 0.9g cm<sup>-3</sup>]
questions.explanation: Volume of ice = 90 / 0.9 = 100 cm3. Volume of water = 90 / 1 = 90 cm3. Change in volume = 100 − 90 = 10 cm3.

questions.question: In a mass spectrometer, an ion of charge, q, and mass, m, moving in a path of radius, r, in a field of flux density, B, has a speed of
questions.explanation: The magnetic force provides the centripetal force: qvB = mv2/r. Rearranging: v = qBr/m.

questions.question: In an experiment in which a molten substance is allowed to cool, the cooling curve above was obtained. The temperature 60<sup>o</sup>C is known as the
questions.explanation: A cooling curve shows a plateau at the temperature where a liquid changes to solid. The plateau at 60°C indicates the temperature at which the molten substance solidifies, i.e., its melting point (freezing point).

questions.question: The velocities of light in air and glass are 3.0 x 10<sup>8</sup>ms<sup>-1</sup> and 2.0 x 10<sup>8</sup>ms<sup>-1</sup> respectively. If the angle of refraction is 30°, the sine of the angle of incidence is?
questions.explanation: By Snell's law: sin i / sin r = vair / vglass. So sin i = (vair/vglass) × sin r = (3.0 × 108 / 2.0 × 108) × sin 30° = 1.5 × 0.5 = 0.75.

questions.question: A mercury-in-glass thermometer reads -20° at the ice point and 100° at the steam point. Calculate the Celsius temperature corresponding to 70° on the thermometer.
What is the frequency of the sound made by a siren having a disc with 32 holes and making 25 revolution per seconds?
questions.explanation: The frequency produced equals the number of holes multiplied by the number of revolutions per second: f = 32 × 25 = 800 Hz.

questions.question: A body moves in SHM between two point 20m on the straight line Joining the points. If the angular speed of the body is 5 rad/s. Calculate its speed when it is 6m from the center of the motion.
questions.explanation: The amplitude A = 20/2 = 10 m. At x = 6 m from centre, the speed is v = ω√(A2 − x2) = 5 × √(102 − 62) = 5 × √64 = 5 × 8 = 40 m/s.

questions.question: Which of the following machines does NOT apply the lever principle?
questions.explanation: A single moving pulley works on the principle of moments but is classified as a pulley system, not a lever. Claw hammer, wheelbarrow, sugar tongs, and nutcrackers are all levers.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct? Sound waves travel through I. air II. vacuum III. Water
questions.explanation: Sound waves are mechanical waves requiring a material medium. They travel through air and water but not through a vacuum. So I and III are correct.

questions.question: Two objects of masses 80kg and 50kg are separated by a distance of 0.2m. If the gravitational constant is 6.6 x 10<sup>-11</sup>Nm<sup>2</sup> kg<sup>-2</sup>, calculate the gravitational attraction between them.
The limiting frictional force between two surfaces depends on I. the cohesive force of the material II. the nature of the surfaces in contact III. the relative velocity between the surfaces
questions.explanation: The limiting frictional force depends on the nature of the surfaces in contact and the normal reaction between them. It is independent of the area of contact and the relative velocity.

questions.question: If the fraction of the atoms of a radioactive material left after 120 years is 1/64, what is the half-life of the material?
questions.explanation: 1/64 = (1/2)6, so 6 half-lives have elapsed. Half-life = 120/6 = 20 years.

questions.question: The amount of energy released when 0.5kg of uranium is burnt completely is [c = 3 x 10<sup>8</sup>m/s]
What is the electric potential at a point distance r from a proton of charge q placed in a medium of permittivity ε<sub>o</sub>?
questions.explanation: The electric potential due to a point charge q at distance r is V = q/(4πεor).

questions.question: A ball of mass 5.0kg hits a smooth vertical wall normally with a speed of 2ms<sup>-1</sup> and rebounds with the same speed. Determine the impulse experienced by the ball
questions.explanation: Impulse = change in momentum = m(v − (−v)) = 2mv = 2 × 5 × 2 = 20 kg m/s.

questions.question: Three non-parallel coplanar forces which can be represented both in magnitude and direction by the three sides of a triangle taken in order will
options: have any one force being the equilibrant of the other two
move a body along a straight line
rotate a body about its axis
questions.explanation: When three coplanar forces are in equilibrium and are represented by the sides of a triangle taken in order, each force is the equilibrant of the other two.

questions.question: Radio waves travel in air at 3.0 x 10<sup>8</sup>ms<sup>-1</sup>. If the waves enter water of refractive index 4/3, calculate the speed of radio waves in water
questions.explanation: Refractive index n = c/v. So v = c/n = (3 × 108)/(4/3) = 3 × 108 × 3/4 = 2.25 × 108 m/s.

questions.question: Determine the focal length of a thin converging lens if the power is 5.0 dioptres
questions.explanation: Power P = 1/f (in metres). So f = 1/P = 1/5 = 0.2 m.

questions.question: A voltage of 240V is connected to the primary coil of a transformer, the rating of the primary turns to the secondary turns if the voltage available at the secondary coil is 15V
questions.explanation: Vp/Vs = Np/Ns. So Np/Ns = 240/15 = 16.

questions.question: Primary colours of light are
questions.explanation: The primary colours of light are red, blue, and green. Cyan, magenta, and yellow are secondary colours.

questions.question: Which of the following concept is not an evidence of the particle nature of matter?
questions.explanation: Crystallization is not evidence of the particle nature of matter. Diffusion, Brownian motion, and diffraction are evidence.

questions.question: A cell of emf 1.5V is connected in series with a 1Ω resistor and a current of 0.3A flows through the resistor. Find the internal resistance of the cell
Which of the following instruments is best for measuring the diameter of a thin constantan wire?
questions.explanation: A micrometer screw gauge has the smallest least count (0.01 mm) and is best for measuring the diameter of thin wires.

questions.question: Calculate the time taken to heat 2kg of water from 50°C to 100°C in an electric kettle taking 5A, from a 210V supply. (Specific heat capacity of water = 4200Jkg<sup>-1</sup>K<sup>-1</sup>)
A generator manufacturing company accidentally made an AC generator instead of a DC generator. To fix this error,
options: the magnetic field needs to be made stronger
the split rings should be replaced with slip rings
the number of turns of the armature coil needs to be decreased
the slip rings should be replaced with split rings
questions.explanation: To convert an AC generator to a DC generator, the slip rings should be replaced with split rings (commutator), which converts alternating current to direct current.

questions.question: A block and tackle pulley arrangement has 6 pulleys in which an effort of 50N supports a load of 200N, calculate the efficiency of the machine
questions.explanation: Velocity ratio (V.R.) = number of pulleys = 6. Mechanical advantage (M.A.) = Load/Effort = 200/50 = 4. Efficiency = (M.A./V.R.) × 100% = (4/6) × 100% = 66.7%.

questions.question: The phenomenon of radioactivity was first discovered by
questions.explanation: Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896 while studying uranium salts.

questions.question: A body is launched from the earth's surface, of radius R, so that it just escapes from the gravitational influence of the earth; If the gravitational constant is G and the mass of the earth is M, what is the escape velocity of the body.
questions.explanation: The escape velocity is vesc = √(2GM/R).

questions.question: An effort of 40N is applied on a machine to lift a mass of 60kg. Determine the mechanical advantage of the machine [g = 10ms<sup>-2</sup>]
questions.explanation: Load = mg = 60 × 10 = 600 N. Mechanical Advantage = Load/Effort = 600/40 = 15.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the laws of solid friction?
options: The frictional force between two surfaces opposes their relative motion
The ratio of frictional force to the normal reaction varies for two given surfaces
The ratio of frictional force to the normal reaction is constant for two given surfaces
The limiting frictional force is independent of the area of surface in contact.
Dynamic frictional force is independent of the relative velocity of the surfaces in contact.
questions.explanation: The ratio of frictional force to normal reaction is constant for two given surfaces, not varying. So statement B is NOT a law of solid friction.

questions.question: Two different materials, rubbed against each other acquired opposite charges when separated. This is an example of charging by
questions.explanation: Charging by friction occurs when two different materials are rubbed together, causing transfer of electrons from one material to the other.

questions.question: A hose of cross-sectional area 0.5m<sup>2</sup> is used to discharge water from a water tanker at a velocity of 60ms<sup>-1</sup> in 20s into a container. If the container is filled completely, the volume of the container is
questions.explanation: Volume flow rate = A × v = 0.5 × 60 = 30 m3/s. In 20 s, volume = 30 × 20 = 600 m3.

questions.question: I. The number of neutrons released exceeds the number that caused the fission. II. There is loss of mass. III. Energy is produced. IV. Smaller nuclei merge to form larger nuclei. Which of the statement above are correct about nuclear fission?
questions.explanation: In nuclear fission: I. More neutrons are released than absorbed. II. Mass is lost (converted to energy). III. Energy is produced. IV is incorrect (that describes fusion). So I, II, and III are correct.

questions.question: A narrow beam of white light can be split up into different Colours by a glass prism. The correct explanation is that
options: white light Is an electromagnetic wave
the prism has all the colours of the white light
different colours of white light travel with different speeds in glass
white light has undergone total Internal reflection in the prism
questions.explanation: Dispersion occurs because different colours of light travel at different speeds in glass, so they refract by different amounts.

questions.question: A cell of e.m.f. 1.5v is connected in series with a resistor of 3Ω. A high resistance voltmeter connected across the cell registers only 0.9v. Calculate the internal resistance of the cell
In which of the following fields is repulsion NOT experienced?
questions.explanation: Gravitational force is always attractive; it never repels. Electric and magnetic forces can both attract and repel.

questions.question: The electrochemical equivalent of a metal is 0.126 x 10<sup>-6</sup> kgC<sup>-1</sup>. The mass of the metal that a current of 5A will deposit from a suitable bath in 1 hour is
The range of wavelengths of the visible spectrum is 400nm - 700nm. The wavelength of gamma rays is
questions.explanation: Gamma rays have wavelengths shorter than 400 nm, typically less than 10-11 m.

questions.question: What is the acceleration of a particle whose motion is graphically displayed in the diagram above
questions.explanation: Acceleration = change in velocity / time = (8.7 − 2.0) / (10 − 0) = 6.7/10 = 0.67 m/s2.

questions.question: A swinging pendulum between the rest position and its maximum displacement possesses
questions.explanation: A swinging pendulum possesses both kinetic and potential energy. At the rest position, it has maximum kinetic energy and minimum potential energy; at maximum displacement, it has maximum potential energy and zero kinetic energy.

questions.question: In an electric circuit, an inductor of inductance 0.5 H and resistance 50Ω is connected to an alternating current source of frequency 60 Hz. Calculate the impedance of the circuit.
questions.explanation: Inductive reactance XL = 2πfL = 2π × 60 × 0.5 = 60π ≈ 188.5 Ω. Impedance Z = √(R2 + XL2) = √(502 + 188.52) = √(2500 + 35532) = √38032 ≈ 195.0 Ω.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions occur at resonance in a series RLC circuit? i. Impedance equals resistance ii. Current is maximum iii. Reactance is maximum iv. Current and voltage are 90° out of phase
questions.explanation: At resonance: impedance equals resistance (i), current is maximum (ii). Reactance is not maximum (it cancels out), and current and voltage are in phase, not 90° out of phase. So i and ii are correct.

questions.question: Lenz's law of electromagnet states that
options: the induced charge is constant for a fixed change of force
a force is exerted on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
the magnitude of the induced e.m.f in a circuit is proportional to the rate of change of the number of lines of force linking the circuit
the induced current in a conductor is in such a direction as to oppose the change producing it
e.m.f. is induced in a circuit whenever there is a change in the magnetic flux linked with the circuit
questions.explanation: Lenz's law states that the induced current flows in such a direction as to oppose the change producing it.

questions.question: A process by which two light atoms join to form a new atom of higher atomic mass is
questions.explanation: Nuclear fusion is the process where two light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy.

questions.question: The major difference between a pure semiconductor and a pure metal is that
options: while resistance of metals decrease with temperature, the reverse is the case for semiconductor
the resistance of metals increases with temperature, while for semiconductors, it is the reverse
metals have forbidden gaps while semiconductors have not
questions.explanation: For metals, resistance increases with temperature. For semiconductors, resistance decreases with temperature.

questions.question: The diagram above shows a magnet X with its south pole moved along a soft-iron bar PQ in the direction shown. After some time, the poles at P and Q respectively are
questions.explanation: When the south pole of a magnet approaches P, it induces a north pole at P. By magnetic induction, Q becomes a south pole. So P = North, Q = South.

questions.question: An electric iron is rated 1000W, 230V. What is the resistance of its elements?

An object weighing 0.60N is hung on a spiral spring and caused it to extend by 6.0cm. The object is removed and a block of wood replacing it causes the spring to extend by 10.0cm. What is the weight of the block of wood?
questions.explanation: From Hooke's law, F = ke. First case: 0.6 = k × 0.06 → k = 10 N/m. Second case: F = k × 0.10 = 10 × 0.10 = 1.00 N.

questions.question: In a Daniel cell, the depolarizer, positive and negative electrodes are respectively
options: sulphuric acid, lead oxide and lead
questions.explanation: In a Daniel cell: depolarizer = copper sulphate solution, positive electrode = copper, negative electrode = zinc.

questions.question: A particle of charge q and mass m moving with a velocity v enters a uniform magnetic field B in the direction of the field. The force on the particle is
questions.explanation: The force on a charged particle in a magnetic field is F = qvB sin θ. When the particle moves in the direction of the field, θ = 0°, so sin θ = 0, giving F = 0. However, the question asks for the force formula. The maximum force is F = Bqv when θ = 90°. The answer is Bqv.

questions.question: An object 3.0cm high is placed 60.0cm from a converging lens whose focal length is 20.0cm. Calculate the size of the image formed
Which of the following bodies, each with centre of gravity G, lying on a horizontal table, is/are in unstable equilibrium?
questions.explanation: A body is in unstable equilibrium when a slight displacement raises its centre of gravity. Body III has its centre of gravity at the highest point, so it is in unstable equilibrium.

questions.question: The lower and upper fixed points of a mercury-in-glass thermometer are marked Y and 180mm respectively. On a particular the mercury meniscus in the thermometer rises to 45mm. If the corresponding reading on a scale is 10°, calculate the value of Y.
In the diagram shown, If the south-poles of two magnets stroke a steel bar, the polarities at T and V will respectively be
questions.explanation: When the south poles of two magnets stroke a steel bar, both ends become north poles due to magnetic induction. So T and V are both north.

questions.question: A particle of charge q and mass m moving with a velocity v enters a uniform magnetic field B in the direction of the field. The force on the particle is
questions.explanation: The force on a charged particle moving in a magnetic field is F = qvB sin θ. When the particle moves parallel to the field, θ = 0°, so sin θ = 0, and F = 0. The maximum force is F = Bqv when the particle moves perpendicular to the field.

questions.question: An object 3.0cm high is placed 60.0cm from a converging lens whose focal length is 20.0cm. Calculate the size of the image formed

The lower and upper fixed points of a mercury-in-glass thermometer are marked Y and 180mm respectively. On a particular the mercury meniscus in the thermometer rises to 45mm. If the corresponding reading on a scale is 10°, calculate the value of Y.
In the diagram shown, If the south-poles of two magnets stroke a steel bar, the polarities at T and V will respectively be
questions.explanation: When the south poles of two magnets stroke a steel bar, both ends become north poles due to magnetic induction. So T and V are both north.

questions.question: Which process is responsible for production of energy in stars?
questions.explanation: Nuclear fusion is the process in which lighter nuclei combine to form heavier ones. The mass lost in this process is converted into energy according to E = mc2. This is the source of energy in stars, including the sun, where hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium.

questions.question: The velocity of a sound wave at 27°C is 360ms<sup>-1</sup>. Its velocity at 127°C is
questions.explanation: Velocity of sound is proportional to the square root of absolute temperature: v ∝ √T. So v2/v1 = √(T2/T1). T1 = 27 + 273 = 300 K, T2 = 127 + 273 = 400 K. v2 = 360 × √(400/300) = 360 × √(4/3) = 360 × 2/√3 = 720/√3 = 720√3/3 = 240√3 m/s.

questions.question: Which of the following substances is not an insulator?
questions.explanation: Aluminium is a metal and a good conductor of electricity and heat. Insulators include glass, plastic, clay, and cork.

questions.question: A rainbow is formed when sunlight is incident on water droplets suspended in the air due to
questions.explanation: A rainbow is formed due to dispersion of sunlight by water droplets. Different colours of light refract by different amounts, separating into the spectrum.

questions.question: The frequency of a body executing simple harmonic motion when left undisturbed is known as__________ frequency.
questions.explanation: The frequency at which a body vibrates freely without any external periodic force is called its natural frequency.

questions.question: Which of the following equations shows how the linear expansivity (α) and the cubic expansivity (γ) of a material are related?
questions.explanation: The cubic expansivity (γ) is three times the linear expansivity (α): γ = 3α.

questions.question: The constant temperature at which a liquid change into gaseous state is known as
questions.explanation: The boiling point is the constant temperature at which a liquid changes into its gaseous state throughout its volume.

questions.question: Determine the inductive reactance when a 30.0mH inductor with a negligible resistance is connected to a 1.3 x 10<sup>3</sup>Hz oscillator.
questions.explanation: Inductive reactance XL = 2πfL = 2 × 3.142 × 1.3 × 103 × 30 × 10-3 = 2 × 3.142 × 39 = 245 Ω.

questions.question: In the diagram above, what would happen to the current I, if another resistor, R<sub>2</sub>, is connected in parallel to R<sub>1</sub>?
options: It will increase because the equivalent resistance will increase
It will decrease if R<sub>2</sub> is greater than R<sub>1</sub>
It will increase because the effective resistance will decrease
It will decrease if R<sub>2</sub> is less than R<sub>1</sub>
questions.explanation: Adding a resistor in parallel always decreases the effective resistance. Since I = V/R, a decrease in resistance causes an increase in current.

questions.question: The magnitude of the force required to make an object of mass M move with speed V in a circular path of radius R is given by the expression.
questions.explanation: The centripetal force required for circular motion is F = mv2/r.

questions.question: If a load of 1 kg stretches a cord by 1.2cm, what is the force constant of the cord? {g=10ms<sup>-2</sup>}
questions.explanation: Force F = mg = 1 × 10 = 10 N. Extension e = 1.2 cm = 0.012 m. Force constant k = F/e = 10/0.012 = 833 N/m.

questions.question: In which of the following are the substances arranged in descending order of their thermal conductivities?
questions.explanation: Thermal conductivity: copper > steel > glass. So the descending order is copper, steel, glass.

questions.question: As per Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction, an e.m.f is induced in a conductor whenever
options: lies parallel to the magnetic flux
lies outside but close to a magnetic field
questions.explanation: An e.m.f. is induced when a conductor cuts magnetic flux (i.e., when there is a change in the magnetic flux linked with the conductor).

questions.question: A girl stands 80m away from a tall cliff and blows a whistle. If the speed of sound in air is 330ms<sup>-1</sup>, how long would it take for her to hear the echo of the sound?
questions.explanation: Total distance = 2 × 80 = 160 m. Time = distance/speed = 160/330 = 0.485 s.

questions.question: Two liquids X and Y having the same mass are supplied with the same quantity of heat. If the temperature rise in X is twice that of Y, the ratio of specific heat capacity of X to that of Y is
questions.explanation: Q = mcΔθ. Since Q and m are the same, cXΔθX = cYΔθY. Given ΔθX = 2ΔθY, so cX(2ΔθY) = cYΔθY → 2cX = cY → cX:cY = 1:2.

questions.question: A body is rotating in a horizontal circle of radius 2.5m with an angular speed of 5 rad s<sup>-1</sup>. Calculate the magnitude of the radial acceleration of the body
questions.explanation: Radial (centripetal) acceleration a = ω2r = 52 × 2.5 = 25 × 2.5 = 62.5 m/s2.

questions.question: Which of these is a derived unit?
questions.explanation: The newton is a derived unit (force = mass × acceleration = kg·m/s2). Kilogram, metre, and second are fundamental units.

questions.question: A nuclide X is produced by bombarding a nitrogen(N) nucleus with an alpha(α) particle with the release of heavy hydrogen(D) nucleus as shown by the following nuclear equation, α + <sup>14</sup><sub>7</sub>N → <sup>p</sup><sub>q</sub>X + <sup>2</sup><sub>1</sub>D. Determine the values of p and q in the equation
questions.explanation: Balancing mass numbers: 4 + 14 = p + 2 → p = 16. Balancing atomic numbers: 2 + 7 = q + 1 → q = 8. So p = 16, q = 8.

questions.question: If the length of a simple pendulum is 120cm, calculate its frequency [π = 22/7, g = 10ms<sup>-2</sup>]
A blacksmith heated a metal whose cubic expansivity is 6.3 x 10<sup>-6</sup>K<sup>-1</sup>. The area expansivity is
questions.explanation: Cubic expansivity γ = 3α, where α is linear expansivity. Area expansivity β = 2α. Given γ = 6.3 × 10-6 K-1, so α = γ/3 = 2.1 × 10-6 K-1. Then β = 2α = 2 × 2.1 × 10-6 = 4.2 × 10-6 K-1.

questions.question: The main difference between echo and reverberation is that
options: reverberation is reflected sound while echo is refracted sound
the time interval between incident sound and reflected sound is shorter for reverberation
the amplitude of an echo is greater
reverberation is from acoustic speakers while echo comes from cliffs
questions.explanation: In reverberation, the reflected sound arrives so quickly that it cannot be distinguished from the original sound. In echo, the time interval is long enough to hear the reflected sound as a separate sound.

questions.question: The half-life of a radioactive substance is 15 hours. If at some instance, the sample has a mass of 512 g, calculate the time it will take 7/8 of the sample to decay
questions.explanation: If 7/8 decays, then 1/8 remains. 1/8 = (1/2)3, so 3 half-lives have elapsed. Time = 3 × 15 = 45 hours.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an electromagnetic radiation?
questions.explanation: Sound waves are mechanical waves and are not electromagnetic radiation. X-rays, radio waves, sunlight, and infrared are all electromagnetic waves.

questions.question: The diagram above illustrates the wire connections to a three-pin plug. The wires P, Q and R respectively are:
questions.explanation: In a standard three-pin plug, the wires are connected as follows: P = neutral, Q = earth, R = live.

questions.question: A body weighing 10 N in air is partially immersed in water. It displaces water of mass 0.3 kg. What is the upthrust on the body? (g = 10 ms<sup>-2</sup>)
questions.explanation: Upthrust = weight of water displaced = mg = 0.3 × 10 = 3.0 N.

questions.question: A cell can supply current of 0.8A and 0.4A through a 2Ω and a 3Ω resistors respectively. Calculate the internal resistance of the cell.
questions.explanation: Let internal resistance be r. For first case: E = 0.8(2 + r). For second: E = 0.4(3 + r). Equating: 0.8(2 + r) = 0.4(3 + r) → 1.6 + 0.8r = 1.2 + 0.4r → 0.4r = -0.4 → r = 1.0 Ω.

questions.question: An electric iron is rated at 1000watts, 250v. The corresponding maximum resistance and accompanying current is
Calculate the electric potential at a distance of 20.0cm from a point charge of 0.015C placed in air of permittivity (Take 1/4πε<sub>o</sub> as 9.0 x 10<sup>9</sup> Nm<sup>2</sup>C<sup>-2</sup>)
Which of the following optical instruments does not depend on the use of plane mirrors?
questions.explanation: A simple microscope uses a convex lens, not plane mirrors. Kaleidoscope, sextant, and periscope use plane mirrors.

questions.question: What is the effective capacitance in the circuit?
questions.explanation: Three 6μF capacitors in series: 1/C = 1/6 + 1/6 + 1/6 = 3/6 = 1/2 → C = 2 μF.

questions.question: A 10 Ω coil takes 21 s to melt 10g of ice at 0°C. Assuming no heat losses, determine the current in the coil. (Specific latent heat of fusion of ice = 336 Jg<sup>-1</sup>)
questions.explanation: Heat supplied = I2Rt = heat required to melt ice = mL. So I2 × 10 × 21 = 10 × 336 → I2 = 3360/210 = 16 → I = 4 A.

questions.question: A luminous object is one that
options: gives off dim blue-green light only in the dark
gives out light of its own
glows only in the presence of light
questions.explanation: A luminous object is one that emits light of its own, such as the sun, a burning candle, or a light bulb.

questions.question: A platinum resistance thermometer has a resistance 4Ω at 0°C and 10Ω at 100°C. Assuming the resistance changes uniformly with temperature. Calculate the resistance of the thermometer when the temperature is 45°C.
When an atom loses or gains a charge it becomes
questions.explanation: When an atom loses or gains electrons, it becomes an ion. Loss of electrons gives a positive ion; gain of electrons gives a negative ion.

questions.question: Two forces forming a couple are separated by a distance of 25cm. If one of the forces equals 40N, what is the moment of the couple?
questions.explanation: Moment of a couple = force × perpendicular distance = 40 × 0.25 = 10 Nm.

questions.question: The half-life of a radioactive substance is 2 seconds. Calculate the decay constant
questions.explanation: Decay constant λ = 0.693/T1/2 = 0.693/2 = 0.347 s-1.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the energy changes which take place when a steam engine drives a generator which lights a lamp?
options: heat → Kinetic → Electricity → Heat and Light
questions.explanation: Steam engine: heat energy → kinetic energy (mechanical). Generator: kinetic energy → electrical energy. Lamp: electrical energy → heat and light energy. So heat → kinetic → electricity → heat and light.

questions.question: When the temperature of a liquid increases, its surface tension
questions.explanation: Surface tension decreases as temperature increases because the increased kinetic energy of molecules weakens the cohesive forces.

questions.question: Light of energy 5.0 eV falls on a metal of work function 3.0 eV and electrons are emitted, determine the stopping potential. [electronic charge, e = 1.60 x 10<sup>-19</sup>C]
questions.explanation: Einstein's photoelectric equation: hf = W + eVs. So eVs = hf − W = 5.0 − 3.0 = 2.0 eV. Therefore Vs = 2.0 V.

questions.question: During a thunderstorm, the sound is heard over a long time. this phenomenon is referred to as?
questions.explanation: Reverberation is the persistence of sound due to multiple reflections, causing the sound to be heard over a prolonged period.

questions.question: In which of the following diagrams is the length of the tube equal to one wavelength?
questions.explanation: For a tube closed at one end, the fundamental frequency has length L = λ/4. For the first overtone, L = 3λ/4. The diagram showing L = λ corresponds to the second overtone in a closed pipe or the first overtone in an open pipe.

questions.question: A light wave of frequency 5 x 10<sup>14</sup>Hz moves through water which has a refractive index of 4/3. Calculate the wavelength in water if the velocity of light in air is 3 x 10<sup>8</sup>ms<sup>-1</sup>
questions.explanation: Speed of light in water = c/n = (3 × 108)/(4/3) = 2.25 × 108 m/s. Wavelength λ = v/f = (2.25 × 108)/(5 × 1014) = 4.5 × 10-7 m.

questions.question: Which of the following statements are true of an insulated charged body carrying positive charge? i. it contains excess positive charges. ii. it creates an electric field. iii. it possesses potential energy. iv. it carries electric current.
questions.explanation: An insulated charged body with positive charge: (i) has excess positive charges, (ii) creates an electric field, (iii) possesses potential energy. It does not carry electric current (iv) because there is no continuous flow of charge. So i, ii, and iii are correct.

questions.question: A metal of mass 0.5kg is heated to 100°C and then transferred to a well-lagged calorimeter of heat capacity 80JK<sup>-1</sup> containing water of heat capacity 420JK<sup>-1</sup> at 15°C. If the final steady temperature of the mixture is 25°C, find the specific heat capacity of the metal.
questions.explanation: Heat lost by metal = heat gained by calorimeter + water. 0.5 × c × (100 − 25) = 80 × (25 − 15) + 420 × (25 − 15) → 37.5c = 800 + 4200 = 5000 → c = 5000/37.5 = 133 J kg-1 K-1.

questions.question: A transistor function mainly as a
questions.explanation: A transistor is mainly used as a switch and an amplifier in electronic circuits.

questions.question: In the diagram above, a rod 50 cm long of uniform cross-section is suspended horizontally on a fulcrum, F, by the action of two forces. What is the weight of the rod?
questions.explanation: Taking moments about the fulcrum: 200 × 10 = W × 10 + 40 × 30. So 2000 = 10W + 1200 → 10W = 800 → W = 80 N.

questions.question: A siren having a ring of 200 holes makes 132 rev/min. A jet of air is directed on the set of holes. Calculate the frequency and wavelength in air of the note produced (take v = 350m/s)
questions.explanation: Frequency f = number of holes × revolutions per second = 200 × (132/60) = 200 × 2.2 = 440 Hz. Wavelength λ = v/f = 350/440 = 0.795 m.

questions.question: The electric field intensity in a place where a charge of 10<sup>-10</sup>C experiences a force of 0.4N is?
The diagram above illustrates the velocity-time graph of the motion of a body. Calculate the total distance covered by the body
questions.explanation: Distance = area under graph. Area A (triangle) = ½ × (10 + 20) × 5 = 75 m. Area B (rectangle) = 20 × 5 = 100 m. Area C (triangle) = ½ × 5 × 20 = 50 m. Total = 75 + 100 + 50 = 225 m.

questions.question: According to kinetic molecular model, in gases
options: The particles are closely packed together, they occupy minimum space & are usually arranged in a regular pattern
The particles occur in clusters with molecules slightly farther apart
The molecules are very fast apart & occupy all the space made available
The particles vibrate about fixed positions and are held together by the strong intermolecular bonds between them
questions.explanation: In gases, molecules are far apart and move randomly at high speeds, occupying all available space.

questions.question: A brass rod is 2 m long at a certain temperature. Calculate the linear expansion of the rod for a temperature change of 100 K. (Take linear expansivity of brass as 1.8 × 10<sup>-5</sup> K<sup>-1</sup>)
It is known that a neutron exists in a light atomic nucleus. Which of the following also exists in the nucleus?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons. Electrons and beta particles are not found in the nucleus (beta particles are emitted from it).

questions.question: Which of the following physical processes cannot be explained by the molecular theory of matter?
questions.explanation: Radiation of heat involves energy transfer by electromagnetic waves and does not require a material medium, so it cannot be explained by the molecular theory of matter.

questions.question: After reflection from the concave mirror, rays of light from the sun converges
options: between the focus and radius of curvature
questions.explanation: Rays from the sun are parallel. A concave mirror converges parallel rays at the focus.

questions.question: When two like charges are brought together, the potential energy of the system formed will
options: increase because work is done against the field
increase because work is done by the field
decrease because work is done by the field
decrease because work is done against the field
questions.explanation: Like charges repel. Bringing them closer requires work done against the repulsive force, so the potential energy increases.

questions.question: An inductor of inductance 1.0H is connected in series with a capacitor of capacitance 2.0μF in an a.c. circuit. to resonate,
The volume of an air bubble increases from the bottom to the top of a lake at constant temperature because
options: atmospheric pressure acts on the surface of the lake
questions.explanation: As the bubble rises, the pressure decreases (since pressure increases with depth). By Boyle's law, at constant temperature, decreasing pressure causes the volume to increase.

questions.question: A gas is cooled at a constant pressure from 57°C was observed to shrink one-fifth (1/5) of its original volume of 2.00cm<sup>3</sup>. Find its new temperature
questions.explanation: Using Charles's law: V1/T1 = V2/T2. T1 = 57 + 273 = 330 K. V2 = (1/5)V1. So T2 = T1 × (V2/V1) = 330 × 1/5 = 66 K. In Celsius: 66 − 273 = −207°C.

questions.question: The diagram above illustrates a block and tackle pulley system in which an effort E supports a load of 100.0N. If the efficiency of the machine is 75%, calculate the value of E
questions.explanation: V.R. = 6 (number of pulleys). Efficiency = (M.A./V.R.) × 100 → 75 = (M.A./6) × 100 → M.A. = 4.5. M.A. = Load/Effort → 4.5 = 100/E → E = 22.2 N.

questions.question: Two bodies have masses in the ratio 3:1. They experience forces which impart to them acceleration in the ratio 2:9 respectively. Find the ratio of forces the masses experienced.
questions.explanation: F = ma. F1 = 3 × 2 = 6. F2 = 1 × 9 = 9. Ratio F1:F2 = 6:9 = 2:3.

questions.question: A conductor of length 2m carries a current of 0.8A while kept in a magnetic field of magnetic flux density 0.5T. The maximum force acting on it is
questions.explanation: Maximum force F = BIL = 0.5 × 0.8 × 2 = 0.8 N.

questions.question: 0.5kg of water at 10°C is completely converted to ice by extracting 188000J of heat from it. If the specific heat capacity of water is 4200J kg<sup>-1</sup>C<sup>-1</sup>, calculate the specific latent heat of fusion of ice.
questions.explanation: Heat extracted = heat to cool water from 10°C to 0°C + heat to freeze water at 0°C. 188000 = 0.5 × 4200 × 10 + 0.5 × L → 188000 = 21000 + 0.5L → 0.5L = 167000 → L = 334000 J/kg = 334 kJ/kg.

questions.question: Which of the following descriptions of the image formed by a plane mirror is not correct. the image is----
options: erect and of the same size as the object
laterally inverted and of the same size as the object
erect and bigger than the object
virtual and of the same size
questions.explanation: A plane mirror always forms an image that is the same size as the object. It is not bigger.

questions.question: The air column in a resonance tube is set into resonance by a vibrating tuning fork. The resultant waves in the air column will be
questions.explanation: In a resonance tube, the sound waves form a stationary longitudinal wave due to superposition of incident and reflected waves.

questions.question: I. Low pressure. II. High pressure. III. High p.d. IV. Low p.d. Which combination of the above is true of the conduction of electricity through gases?
questions.explanation: Gases conduct electricity at low pressure and high potential difference. So I and III are correct.

questions.question: Thermal equilibrium between two object exist when
options: the temperature of both objects are equal
the quantity of heat of both objects is the same
the heat capacities of both objects are the same
one object losses heat continuously to the other
questions.explanation: Two objects are in thermal equilibrium when they are at the same temperature and no net heat flows between them.

questions.question: The velocity ratio and efficiency of a system of pulleys are 6 and 80% respectively. How much effort is required to lift a load of mass 120kg with this system? (g=10ms<sup>-2</sup>)
A radioactive element has a decay constant of 0.077s<sup>-1</sup>. Calculate its half-life
If the distance between two stationary charged particle is doubled, the magnitude of the electro-static force between them will be
options: a quarter of its former value
questions.explanation: Coulomb's law: F ∝ 1/r2. If r is doubled, F becomes 1/4 of its original value, i.e., a quarter.

questions.question: The degree of precision of a vernier caliper is
questions.explanation: A standard vernier caliper has a least count (degree of precision) of 0.01 cm or 0.1 mm.

questions.question: A point charge of 1.0 x 10<sup>-7</sup> C experiences force of 0.01 N in a uniform electric field. Calculate the magnitude of the strength of the field
A well 1km deep is filled with a liquid of density 950kg/m<sup>3</sup> and g = 10m/s<sup>2</sup>, the pressure at the bottom of the well is
Which of the following properties of a long steel bar would alter if the bar were melted, recast into a cube and allowed to cool to its original temperature?
questions.explanation: When the steel bar is melted and recast into a cube, its volume changes shape but the mass remains the same, so density stays the same. Specific heat capacity is a material property and remains constant. Electrical resistance depends on shape and size, so it changes. But the question asks which would alter - volume changes from the original bar shape to a cube shape.

questions.question: In which of the following is a stationary wave produced? i. A vibrating tuning fork held near the end of a resonance tube closed at one end. ii. A string tightly stretched between two points and plucked at its middle. iii. The tuning fork vibrating in air
questions.explanation: Stationary waves are produced in: (i) a resonance tube closed at one end, and (ii) a stretched string plucked at its middle. A tuning fork vibrating in air produces progressive waves, not stationary waves. So i and ii are correct.

questions.question: The force responsible for holding the moon in its orbit around the earth against the gravitational pull of the earth is
questions.explanation: The centripetal force (provided by gravitational attraction) keeps the moon in its orbit around the earth.

questions.question: The device that operates using the magnetic effect of electric current is
questions.explanation: An electric bell works using an electromagnet, which is based on the magnetic effect of electric current.

questions.question: Calculate the force acting on an electron of charge 1.6 x 10<sup>-19</sup>C placed in an electric field of intensity 10<sup>8</sup>Vm<sup>-1</sup>
Which of the following statements about an electromagnet is not correct?
options: its strength depends on the current
its strength depends on the number of turns in its coil
questions.explanation: An electromagnet does not have permanent poles. Its polarity depends on the direction of current flow.

questions.question: A man stands in front of a tall wall and produces a sound. If he receives the echo of the sound two seconds later, calculate his distance from the wall. (The speed of sound in air is 330ms<sup>-1</sup>)
questions.explanation: Total distance = v × t = 330 × 2 = 660 m. Distance to wall = 660/2 = 330 m.

questions.question: The eye defect illustrated by the diagram above is
questions.explanation: The diagram shows the image forming behind the retina, which is characteristic of long sightedness (hypermetropia).

questions.question: An explosion occurs at an altitude of 312 m above the ground. If the air temperature is -10.00°C, how long does it take the sound to reach the ground? [velocity of sound at 0°C = 331 ms<sup>-1</sup>]
questions.explanation: Velocity at temperature T: v = v0√(T/273) = 331 × √(263/273) = 331 × 0.981 = 324.7 m/s. Time = distance/velocity = 312/324.7 = 0.96 s.

questions.question: Which of the following devices may be used to step up the voltage in a d.c. circuit?
questions.explanation: An induction coil can step up voltage in a d.c. circuit by rapidly interrupting the current. A transformer requires alternating current.

questions.question: The circuit contains three ammeters A1, A2 and A3 with readings of A2 and A3 shown as indicated in the diagram. Determine the reading of A1.
questions.explanation: A3 = A1 + A2 (currents in parallel branches add up). A3 = 5A, A2 = 2A. So A1 = 5 − 2 = 3 A.

questions.question: When a potential difference, V is applied across the ends of a resistor of resistance, R a Current, I passes through the resistor. The heat generated in the resistor in time, t is given by the expression
questions.explanation: Heat generated H = I<sup>2</sup>Rt (Joule's law).

questions.question: Two rays of light from a point below the surface of water are equally inclined to each other at 60° in water. What is the angle between the rays when they emerge into air? (Take the refractive index of water to be 4/3)
questions.explanation: Each ray makes 30° with the normal in water. Using Snell's law: (4/3) = sin r / sin 30° → sin r = (4/3) × 0.5 = 0.667 → r = 41.8°. The angle between the two rays in air = 2 × 41.8° = 83.6°.

questions.question: A simple harmonic oscillator has a period of 0.02s and amplitude of 0.25m. Calculate the speed in ms<sup>-1</sup> at the centre of the oscillation
questions.explanation: Maximum speed at the centre = ωA = (2π/T) × A = (2π/0.02) × 0.25 = 100π × 0.25 = 25π m/s.

questions.question: Two parallel plates at a distance of 8.0 x 10<sup>-3</sup>m apart are maintained at a p.d of 600 volts with the negative plate earthed. What is the electric field strength?
A capacitor of 20 x 10<sup>-12</sup>F and an inductor are joined in series. The value of the inductance that will give the circuit a resonance frequency of 200 kHz is
questions.explanation: Resonant frequency f = 1/(2π√(LC)). Rearranging: L = 1/(4π2f2C). Using π2 ≈ 10: L = 1/(4 × 10 × (200 × 103)2 × 20 × 10-12) = 1/(4 × 10 × 4 × 1010 × 20 × 10-12) = 1/(32 × 10-1) = 1/32 H.

questions.question: An object is said to undergo oscillatory motion when it moves
options: to and fro about a fixed point
along a continuous path from the starting point
questions.explanation: Oscillatory motion is motion where an object moves to and fro about a fixed point (equilibrium position).

questions.question: The heating element in an electric kettle is usually located near the bottom of the kettle because
options: water is a good conductor of heat
heat can be more quickly radiated to all parts of the water
no heat can be lost to the surroundings
the convectional currents which are set up can carry heat to all parts of the water
the molecules of the heating element can carry heat to all parts of the water
questions.explanation: The heating element is at the bottom so that convection currents can carry heat throughout the water. Hot water rises and cold water sinks, creating a circulation.

questions.question: The fig above shows the heights of two liquids X and Y when some air is sucked out of the apparatus through the pump P. The diameter of the tube in X is twice that of the tube in Y. What is the relative density of the liquid X with respect to liquid Y?
questions.explanation: Relative density = height of Y / height of X (since pressure is the same). From the diagram, hY = 22.5 cm, hX = 7.5 cm. Relative density = 22.5/7.5 = 3.

questions.question: A stone is dropped from the top of a tower of height 11.25m. Calculate the time it will take to reach the ground. [g = 10ms<sup>-2</sup>]
The area under a force-time graph represents
questions.explanation: The area under a force-time graph gives the impulse, which equals the change in momentum.

questions.question: I. Temperature. II. Density of air molecules III. Pressure IV. Pitch. Which of the above will affect the velocity of sound in the air
questions.explanation: Velocity of sound in air depends on temperature (I) and density of air molecules (II). Pressure does not affect it (since pressure and density effects cancel). Pitch is a property of the sound itself, not the medium. So I and II.

questions.question: A chemical cell of internal resistance 1Ω supplies electric current to an external resistor of resistance 3Ω. Calculate the efficiency of the cell
The design of the thermostat of an electric iron is based on the
options: emission of electrons from metals when heated
increase in size of metals when heated
increase in the density of metals when heated
change in the mass of metals when heated
questions.explanation: A thermostat uses a bimetallic strip that bends due to the increase in size (expansion) of metals when heated.

questions.question: The resultant of two forces acting on an object is maximum if the angle between them is
questions.explanation: The resultant is maximum when the forces act in the same direction, i.e., angle = 0°.

questions.question: Electrolysis can be investigated using
questions.explanation: A voltameter (electrolytic cell) is used to investigate electrolysis.

questions.question: In the image above, an incident ray XY makes an angle of 15° with a fixed line AY, which is normal to surface of a plane mirror. If the mirror is turned as indicated by the arrow through 40°, what angle will the reflected ray make with AY
questions.explanation: When a mirror is rotated by angle θ, the reflected ray rotates by 2θ. Initial angle with AY = 15°. After rotating mirror by 40°, the reflected ray rotates by 80°. New angle = 15° + 80° = 95°.

questions.question: The engine of a car provides a forward force of 1240 N and the total resistive force on the car is 800N. If the mass of the car is 1220 kg, determine the distance the car has to travel from rest before acquiring a speed of 4 m s<sup>-1</sup>
questions.explanation: Net force = 1240 − 800 = 440 N. Acceleration a = F/m = 440/1220 = 0.361 m/s2. Using v2 = u2 + 2as: 42 = 0 + 2 × 0.361 × s → 16 = 0.722s → s = 22.2 m.

questions.question: A block of ice of mass 10kg at 0°C absorbs heat energy from its surroundings and changes to water at the same temperature. The heat absorbed is referred to as
questions.explanation: The heat absorbed during a change of state at constant temperature is latent heat.

questions.question: A converging lens of focal length 10cm forms an erect image three times the size of the real object. Calculate the distance between the image and the object.
questions.explanation: Magnification m = 3 (erect, virtual). Using m = v/u = 3 → v = 3u. Lens formula: 1/f = 1/u − 1/v (virtual image). 1/10 = 1/u − 1/(3u) = 2/(3u) → 3u = 20 → u = 6.67 cm. v = 3u = 20 cm. Distance between image and object = v − u = 20 − 6.67 = 13.3 cm.

questions.question: A car travels with a constant velocity of 45 kmh<sup>-1</sup> for 20s. What distance does it cover in this time?
questions.explanation: Convert speed: 45 km/h = 45 × (1000/3600) = 12.5 m/s. Distance = speed × time = 12.5 × 20 = 250 m.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Alpha particles have a large mass and high penetrating power
Alpha particles have a small mass and a low penetrating power
Beta particles have no mass and a high penetrating power
Beta particles have a large mass and a low penetrating power
Gamma rays have no mass and a high penetrating power
questions.explanation: Gamma rays have no mass and charge, and have the highest penetrating power among alpha, beta, and gamma radiation.

questions.question: A boy timed 30 oscillations of a certain pendulum thrice and obtained 1min. 10s, 1min. 12s and 1min. 7s respectively. The mean period of oscillation of the pendulum is
questions.explanation: Total time for 30 oscillations = (70 + 72 + 67)/3 = 209/3 = 69.67 s. Period = total time / number of oscillations = 69.67/30 = 2.32 s.

questions.question: If the fraction of the atoms of a radioactive material left after 120years is 1/64, what is the half-life of the material?
questions.explanation: 1/64 = (1/2)6, so 6 half-lives. Half-life = 120/6 = 20 years.

questions.question: Water and Kerosine are drawn respectively into the two limbs of a Hare's apparatus. The density of water is 1.0gcm<sup>-3</sup> and the density of kerosine is 0.80gcm<sup>-3</sup>. If the height of the water column is 20.0cm, calculate the height of the kerosine column.
questions.explanation: In Hare's apparatus, ρ1h1 = ρ2h2. 1.0 × 20 = 0.80 × h2 → h2 = 20/0.8 = 25 cm.

questions.question: A radioactive nuclide of mass 6.09g has a half-life of 8 days. Calculate the time during which 5.25g of the nuclide would have decayed
questions.explanation: Mass remaining = 6.09 − 5.25 = 0.84 g. Fraction remaining = 0.84/6.09 ≈ 1/7.25. Using N = N0(1/2)n: 0.84 = 6.09(1/2)n → (1/2)n = 0.138 → n = log(0.138)/log(0.5) ≈ 2.86 half-lives. Time = 2.86 × 8 = 22.9 ≈ 24 days (approximating n = 3).

questions.question: A room is heated by means of a charcoal fire, an occupant of the room standing away from the fire is warmed mainly by
questions.explanation: The occupant is warmed mainly by radiation, which does not require a medium and travels in straight lines.

questions.question: A simple cell with mercury-amalgamated zinc electrode prevents
questions.explanation: Amalgamating the zinc electrode with mercury prevents local action caused by impurities in the zinc.

questions.question: Heat transfer by convection in a liquid is due to the
options: Latent heat of vaporization of the liquid
Increased vibration of the molecules of the liquid about their mean position
Variation of density of the liquid
Expansion of the liquid as it is heated
questions.explanation: Convection occurs due to variation of density within the liquid. Hot liquid expands, becomes less dense, and rises; cold liquid sinks.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of phenomena helps in the resolution of the wave-particle paradox of matter?
questions.explanation: The wave-particle paradox is resolved by phenomena that show both wave and particle properties. The emission and absorption of light demonstrate both wave and particle aspects.

questions.question: A working electric motor takes a current of 1.5 A when the p.d across it is 250V. If its efficiency is 80%, the power output is
questions.explanation: Input power = IV = 1.5 × 250 = 375 W. Efficiency = (output/input) × 100% → 80 = (output/375) × 100 → output = 300 W.

questions.question: The graph above shows the relationship between sin i and sin r for a ray of light in air incident on a liquid surface. If i and r are respectively angles of incidence and refraction, deduce the refractive index of the liquid from the graph
questions.explanation: From Snell's law, n = sin i / sin r = slope of the graph. The graph passes through points (0.08, 0.1) and (0.4, 0.5). Slope = (0.5 − 0.1)/(0.4 − 0.08) = 0.4/0.32 = 1.25.

questions.question: If a wheel 1.2 m in diameter rotates at one revolution per second, calculate the velocity of the wheel.
questions.explanation: Radius r = 1.2/2 = 0.6 m. Angular velocity ω = 2πf = 2π × 1 = 2π rad/s. Velocity v = ωr = 2π × 0.6 = 1.2π = 3.77 m/s.

questions.question: A wire of length 100cm and cross-sectional area of 2.0 x 10<sup>-3</sup>cm<sup>2</sup> has a resistance of 0.10 Ω. Calculate its electrical conductivity.
questions.explanation: Resistivity ρ = RA/L = (0.10 × 2.0 × 10-3)/100 = 2.0 × 10-6 Ω cm. Conductivity σ = 1/ρ = 1/(2.0 × 10-6) = 5.0 × 105 Ω-1 cm-1.

questions.question: A pipe of length 45cm is closed at the end. Calculate the fundamental frequency of the sound wave generated in the pipe if the velocity of sound in air is 360ms<sup>-1</sup> [Neglect end correction]
questions.explanation: For a closed pipe, fundamental frequency f = v/(4L) = 360/(4 × 0.45) = 360/1.8 = 200 Hz.

questions.question: A screw jack with a Tommy bar of length 12cm is used to raise a car through a vertical height of 25cm by turning the Tommy bar through 50 revolutions. Calculate the approximate velocity ratio of the jack [π = 3.142]
The gravitational force between two masses, P and Q, is 10N, find the new value of the force if both masses are doubled
questions.explanation: F = Gm1m2/r2. If both masses are doubled: F' = G(2m1)(2m2)/r2 = 4F = 4 × 10 = 40 N.

questions.question: If the refractive index of crown glass is 1.51, its critical angle is?
A semiconductor diode is used in rectifying alternating current into direct current mainly because it
options: allows current to flow in either direction
allows current to flow only in one direction
questions.explanation: A diode allows current to flow only in one direction, which is the key property for rectification.

questions.question: Particles of mass 10<sup>-2</sup>kg is fixed to the tip of a fan blade which rotates with angular velocity of 100rad/s. If the radius of the blade is 0.2m, the centripetal force is?
questions.explanation: Centripetal force F = mω2r = 10-2 × (100)2 × 0.2 = 10-2 × 10000 × 0.2 = 20 N.

questions.question: The diagram above represents six maximum and minimum thermometer. If the temperature of the surrounding falls, which of the following correctly states how the thermometer would respond to the change in temperature?
options: S<sub>1</sub> would move upward but S<sub>2</sub> would not move
S<sub>1</sub> would not move but S<sub>2</sub> would move upwards
both S<sub>1</sub> and S<sub>2</sub> would move upwards
S<sub>1</sub> would move downwards and S<sub>2</sub> would move downward
S<sub>1</sub> would move downwards and S<sub>2</sub> would not move downwards
questions.explanation: In a maximum-minimum thermometer, when temperature falls, S1 remains in position (maximum) while S2 moves upwards (minimum). So S1 would not move but S2 would move upwards.

questions.question: 4g of a radioactive material of half-life 10 days is spilled on a laboratory floor. How long would it take to disintegrate 3.5g of the material?
questions.explanation: Mass remaining = 4 − 3.5 = 0.5 g. Fraction remaining = 0.5/4 = 1/8 = (1/2)3. So 3 half-lives. Time = 3 × 10 = 30 days.

questions.question: If two inductors of inductances 3H and 6H are arranged in series, the total inductance is
questions.explanation: For inductors in series, Ltotal = L1 + L2 = 3 + 6 = 9 H.

questions.question: What is the resultant capacity of the circuit?
questions.explanation: The 1µF and 5µF are in parallel: Cp = 1 + 5 = 6µF. This 6µF is in series with 4µF and 4µF: 1/C = 1/6 + 1/4 + 1/4 = (2 + 3 + 3)/12 = 8/12 = 2/3 → C = 1.5 µF.

questions.question: If the charge of electricity is K wh is N4, what is the cost of operating an electrical appliance rated 250 v,2 A for six hours?
questions.explanation: Power = IV = 2 × 250 = 500 W = 0.5 kW. Energy = 0.5 × 6 = 3 kWh. Cost = 3 × N4 = N12.

questions.question: Hot water is added to three times its mass of water at 10°C and the resultant temperature is 20°C. What is the initial temperature of the hot water?
questions.explanation: Let mass of hot water = m, mass of cold water = 3m. Heat lost = heat gained: mc(T − 20) = 3mc(20 − 10). Cancel mc: T − 20 = 30 → T = 50°C.

questions.question: A water fall is 420m high. Calculate the difference in temperature of the water between the top and bottom of the water fall. Neglect heat losses (g = 10.0m/s<sup>2</sup>, specific heat capacity of water = 4.20 x 10<sup>3</sup> Jkg<sup>-1</sup>K<sup>-1</sup>)
questions.explanation: Potential energy = heat energy: mgh = mcΔθ. Δθ = gh/c = (10 × 420)/(4.20 × 103) = 4200/4200 = 1.0°C.

questions.question: A magnet is similar to a bipolar charged system in that
options: it consists of two opposite poles - the north and south poles
the earth's magnetic field has a south pole near the geographical north pole and a north pole near the geographical south pole
the force of attraction and repulsion between opposite and between like poles obeys a law for electrostatic charges
questions.explanation: A magnet is similar to a bipolar charged system in that: (A) it has two opposite poles (north and south), and (C) the force between poles obeys an inverse square law similar to electrostatic charges. So A and C.

questions.question: The surfaces of conveyor belts are made rough so as to
options: enable them to carry more load
questions.explanation: Rough surfaces increase friction, which prevents loads from slipping on conveyor belts.

questions.question: The force of attraction between two point masses is 10<sup>-4</sup>N when the distance between them is 0.18m. If the distance is reduced to 0.06m, calculate the force.
questions.explanation: F ∝ 1/r2. F1/F2 = (r2/r1)2. F2 = F1 × (r1/r2)2 = 10-4 × (0.18/0.06)2 = 10-4 × 9 = 9.0 × 10-4 N.

questions.question: The relationship between the period T and the length l of a simple pendulum is T = 2π√(l/g). From experiment data of T and l, one can obtain the following graphs, i. T vs l ii. T vs l<sup>2</sup> iii. T<sup>2</sup> vs l iv. T vs √l v. logT vs logl. Which of the following graphs, are linear?
questions.explanation: From T = 2π√(l/g): T2 = (4π2/g)l, so T2 vs l is linear (iii). T vs √l is linear (iv). log T vs log l is linear (v). So iii, iv, and v are linear.

questions.question: The number of neutrons contained in the nucleus <sup>238</sup><sub>92</sub>U is
questions.explanation: Number of neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 238 − 92 = 146.

questions.question: The following properties of a solid are measured on earth: i. weight ii. specific heat capacity iii. density. Which of the properties will have a different value if measured in space?
questions.explanation: Weight depends on gravitational acceleration, which is different in space. Specific heat capacity and density are intrinsic properties and do not change.

questions.question: The resistance of a series R-C circuit is 5 Ω. If the impedance of the circuit is 13 Ω, calculate the reactance of the capacitor
questions.explanation: Z2 = R2 + XC2. XC = √(Z2 − R2) = √(132 − 52) = √(169 − 25) = √144 = 12 Ω.

questions.question: Beta particles are
questions.explanation: Beta particles are high-speed electrons emitted from a nucleus during beta decay.

questions.question: The cubic expansivity of a certain gas at constant pressure is 1/273 K<sup>-1</sup>. If a given mass of the gas is held at constant pressure and its volume at 0°C is 273m<sup>3</sup>, determine the volume of the gas at 273°C.
A short response time is obtained in a liquid-in-glass thermometer when the
options: liquid is of high density and the bulb is large
bulb is thin-walled and the liquid is a good conductor of heat
questions.explanation: A thermometer responds quickly when the bulb is thin-walled (allowing rapid heat transfer) and the liquid is a good conductor of heat.

questions.question: The distance between two successive crests of a water wave is 0.25m. If a particle on the surface of the water makes four complete vertical oscillations in one second. Calculate the speed of the wave.
questions.explanation: Wavelength λ = 0.25 m. Frequency f = 4 Hz. Speed v = fλ = 4 × 0.25 = 1 m/s.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of a d.c. electric motor?
questions.explanation: A transformer is not part of a d.c. electric motor. A d.c. motor consists of field magnets, armature, commutator, and brushes.

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics of a wave is used in the measurement of the depth of the sea?
questions.explanation: The depth of the sea is measured using reflection of sound waves (echo sounding).

questions.question: Which of the following factors does not increase the rate of evaporation of water in a lake?
options: Increase in the pressure of the atmosphere
Increase in the surface area of the lake
Increase in the speed of the wind
questions.explanation: Increasing atmospheric pressure decreases the rate of evaporation. The other factors (temperature, surface area, wind speed) increase it.

questions.question: What must be connected between the points P and Q to establish a steady current through the incomplete circuit diagram given?
questions.explanation: A cell (source of e.m.f.) is needed to drive a steady current through the circuit.

questions.question: If an object is placed between two parallel plane mirrors with their reflecting surfaces facing each other, how many images of the object will be formed?
questions.explanation: Two parallel plane mirrors facing each other produce an infinite number of images due to multiple reflections.

questions.question: Electrical power is transmitted at a high voltage rather than low voltage because the amount of energy loss is reduced due to
questions.explanation: At high voltage, current is low for the same power. Power loss = I2R, so lower current means less heat dissipation in the transmission lines.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of elementary modern physics?
questions.explanation: Classical mechanics is not part of modern physics. Modern physics includes quantum mechanics, special relativity, and nuclear physics.

questions.question: The quantity of motion of a body is its
questions.explanation: Momentum is the quantity of motion of a body, defined as the product of mass and velocity.

questions.question: The gravitational field intensity at a location X, in space, is two-fifths of its value on the earth's surface. If the weight of an object at X is 4.80N, what is its weight on the earth?
questions.explanation: gX = (2/5)gearth. Weight at X = mgX = 4.80 N. Weight on earth = mgearth = mgX × (5/2) = 4.80 × 2.5 = 12.00 N.

questions.question: A galvanometer with a full-scale deflection of 20 mA is converted to read 8 V by connecting a 395 Ω resistor in series with it. Determine the internal resistance of the galvanometer
questions.explanation: For a voltmeter: V = Ig(Rg + R). 8 = 0.02(Rg + 395) → Rg + 395 = 400 → Rg = 5.0 Ω.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fundamental quantity?
questions.explanation: Length is a fundamental quantity. Speed, density, impulse, and energy are derived quantities.

questions.question: Heat transfer by convection will take place in one the following substance.
questions.explanation: Convection occurs in fluids (liquids and gases). Water is a liquid, so convection can occur in it.

questions.question: An empty density bottle weighs 2 N. if it weighs 5 N when filled with water and 4 N when filled with olive oil, the relative density of olive oil is
questions.explanation: Weight of olive oil = 4 − 2 = 2 N. Weight of equal volume of water = 5 − 2 = 3 N. Relative density = 2/3 = 2/3.

questions.question: The handle of a screw jack is 35 cm long and the pitch of the screw is 0.5 cm. What force must be applied at the end of the handle to lift a load of 2000N, if the efficiency of the jack is 30% [π = 22/7]?

A quantity of steam at 100°C condenses to water at the same temperature by releasing 6.9 x 10<sup>4</sup>J of energy. Calculate the mass of the condensed steam. [specific latent heat of vaporization of water = 2.3 x 10<sup>6</sup> J kg<sup>-1</sup>]
If the fraction of the atoms of a radioactive material left after 120years is 1/64, what is the half-life of the material?
questions.explanation: 1/64 = (1/2)6, so 6 half-lives. Half-life = 120/6 = 20 years.

questions.question: Lenz's law of electromagnetic induction states that
options: e.m.f. is induced in a circuit whenever there is a change in the magnetic flux linked with the circuit
the induced e.m.f. in a circuit is proportional to the rate of change of the number of lines of force linking the circuit
the induced current in a conductor is in such a direction as to oppose the change producing it
a force is exerted in a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
the induced e.m.f. is proportional to the current producing the magnetic flux
questions.explanation: Lenz's law states that the induced current flows in such a direction as to oppose the change producing it.
